nodes.title: Positive Prompt
widgets_values: A hyper-realistic, macro photography shot of a tiny, translucent clockwork jellyfish floating inside a glowing vintage lightbulb. The jellyfish is made of delicate gold gears, iridescent glass filaments, and sapphire-encrusted tentacles. The lightbulb is filled with swirling, bioluminescent turquoise water. Soft amber bokeh light filters through a dark, dusty Victorian study in the background. Extremely detailed, 8k resolution, cinematic lighting, ray-tracing reflections on the glass, whimsical and intricate steampunk aesthetic.

### Usage Tips

Make sure width and height of input images are both divisible by 16 to minimize pixel shift.

Toggle off **Use reference images** to enable **T2I** mode. In **T2I** mode the output image is generated based on text prompt alone and reference images are ignored. The output resolution in **T2I** mode is determined by the dimensions of the **Custom output image**, regardless of whether **Use custom output dimensions** is enabled or not.

Add reference images in the **Reference Images** group. You can use more than three reference images by chaining them together as shown. To disable a reference image, bypass its associated **ReferenceLatent** node.

For local edits (e.g., changing hair color and leaving the rest of the image untouched) draw a mask on **Image 1** using the built-in mask editor (_Ctrl+RMB -> Open in Mask Editor_) and enable **Apply mask from Image 1**. This will apply edits only to the masked area.


Use **Color match strength** > 0.0 (default 1.0) to match the color of the output to **Image 1**. _This trick does not always work, but is worth a try!_

By default, the output image has the same dimensions as **Image 1**. You can define custom output width and height by enabling **Use custom output dimensions** and setting the desired dimensions in the empty **Custom output image**.

**IMPORTANT:** Some combinations of the above settings do not work well together. For example, using custom output dimensions while applying a mask will obviously mess things up. Just experiment and have fun!
